h: The Fire That Wounds Becomes a Wall of Healing

p: In the Pesikta, on this consolation (section 7):
'I, I am He Who consoles you'
this is what the verse says (Hoshea 6:1):
'For He has torn and He will heal us;
He has struck and He will bind us up.'
It is like one who developed a wound
and the physician cut it open, etc.:
go to the one who cut it,
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹאֵל אֶתְכֶם וְכוּלֵּי
and HaKadosh Baruch Hu will redeem you, etc.,
for He is the One Who struck,
and He is the One Who heals;
'Come, let us return to Hashem,' etc.
I am the One Who struck,
'From on high He sent fire into my bones';
and I am the One Who heals:
'I, I am He Who consoles you.'"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (בָּבָא קַמָּא ס, ב)
along the lines of what is said (Bava Kamma 60b):
"I am the One Who kindled fire in Tziyon,
'And He kindled fire in Tziyon,' etc.;
and I am the One Who will in the future
a wall of fire all around,' etc."
they are to protect from every trouble,
But the matter of the wall of fire
it is meant as words of Torah,
And it is called a wall of fire,
"From His right hand a fiery law for them";
is that it is a surrounding light,
And this is what the Pesikta says:
that is, so that everything will be rectified,
along the lines of what is said (Shabbos 89b):
which have been arranged and coming
since the six days of Creation,
they shall become white as snow"
that they will become like merits.
And in the utterance "Bereishis" it is written (Bereishis 1:2):
over the face of the waters,"
(in the Pesikta and in Bereishis Rabbah 2:4):
'And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him.'"
And this is what it says (Yeshayahu 11:1):
"And a shoot shall come forth from the stem of Yishai";
it is written "yatza," without the vav,
when you pour out your heart like water
that is, that he will know
And then, when a person takes to heart
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
(in the Hagahah at the beginning of Orach Chaim);
and through this he will come to teshuvah,
אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה׳ (תְּהִלִּים קיב, א)
"'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem' (Tehillim 112:1)
fortunate is one who does teshuvah
while he is still a man."
And this is the meaning of the pasuk
that is, in order that everything be rectified;
to the deeds of the wicked
so that from everything there would come to be
and according to what is written
"'I am a wall' — this is Torah;
We do not know how, etc.
and this is the aspect of Knesses Yisrael.
And this is what it says:
"For He has torn and He will heal us"
"He has struck and He will bind us up"
that it will not go wrong again;
so that the wound does not spread.
And this was the purpose of "He has torn":
so that the healing would come;
so that through this "He will bind us up,"
so that they will not sin in the future.
And this is what it says:
"For He has torn and He will heal us"
(as is written in the holy Zohar in several places);
and the salvation for the future
which is wholly hidden from all thought,
(in the Midrash Rabbah, Bereishis Rabbah 2:4, and the Pesikta):
for both of them, Torah and teshuvah,
and through both of them will come
and the salvation for the future.
And this is the meaning of
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh
And this is what it says:
"I, I am He Who consoles you":
this is the event at Sinai."

paragraphs.text: Source: Berachos 32b — “אמרה לפניו: רבונו של עולם, הואיל ויש שכחה לפני כסא כבודך, שמא תשכח לי מעשה סיני? אמר לה: ״ואנכי לא אשכחך״.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 94) — “The community of Israel said before Him: Master of the Universe, since there is forgetfulness before the Throne of Your Glory, perhaps You will also forget the events revolving around the revelation at Sinai?
